proof_nl: Let x be any real number. By the definition of the floor function, floor(x) is the greatest integer that is less than or equal to x. In particular, floor(x) itself is an integer satisfying floor(x) ≤ x. Since x was arbitrary, this holds for every real number x.
solver_summary: This is immediate from the definition of the floor function: floor(x) is an integer not exceeding x.
vetter_reason: The proof correctly states the defining property of the floor function and derives floor(x) <= x for an arbitrary real x, which is exactly the lemma. No semantic drift or dependency issues are present.
